proposed_statement_changes.proposed: At every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) at which the constrained tangent space \(\mathcal T_P\) is defined on its actual finite support, the constrained efficient influence function is the coordinatewise orthogonal projection \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}G_p\), and the constrained efficiency bound is \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=E_P\{\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(O)^\top\}\). For every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\), \[a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a=\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.\] Thus the constrained bound is strictly smaller than the saturated bound in direction \(a\) exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\). On a smooth local stratum with constant tangent rank and nonsingular information for independent score coordinates, the projection is computable from a finite score matrix by weighted least squares, and a regular local likelihood or one-step estimator attains this bound pointwise. These conclusions do not establish uniform constrained efficiency over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}\), which neither imposes the date-\(4\) restriction nor buffers constrained score rank or support changes.

prose_updates.tldr:
Four matched active-state slices identify the unnormalized latent-type sublaws among units active at date \(1\), even when a common absorbing state makes all-state terminal factors singular and some units are already absorbed. Spectral projectors fix scale, terminal row sums recover exit probabilities, and a full-row-rank pseudoinverse transports the second active predecessor factor. Absorption plus no anticipation makes initially absorbed units' treatment effects zero, so the type contributions \(
u_j\), at-risk effects \(
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), and aggregate ATT \(	au=\sum_j
u_j\) are point identified over the full broad fiber. The observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface additionally identifies full type masses and conditional type effects. The corrected analytic \(126\)-cell map has a saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded multiplier bands with uniform coverage under singular correlation; fifth-date constrained efficiency is stated only on a separate subclass.

project_justification.gap: Published short-panel Markov-mixture reconstruction and the adjacent transition-independence theorem use rank or positivity hypotheses that exclude a common absorbing terminal row. They also do not characterize the identification elbow created when latent types may contain units already absorbed before the active recovery cut: full conditional type effects can fail even though all aggregate causal effects remain identified.
project_justification.niche: Two active states and one absorbing exit state leave four invertible active minors. Their cycle product identifies common type signatures, stochastic row sums identify unnormalized active masses and exit transitions, and absorption converts the omitted initially absorbed subpopulation from an identification obstacle for aggregates into a zero-effect component.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit projector, row-sum, and pseudoinverse map for active component sublaws, type contributions, at-risk type effects, and the aggregate ATT on the broad absorbing class; a no-initial-absorption corollary for full conditional type effects; the exact sharp-frontier witness; an analytic saturated gradient; and uniform guarded multiplier bands on the enlarged support.

sampling_model.design: Observational two-cohort panel with adoption at date \(3\) for \(D=1\), no adoption for \(D=0\), and an absorbing exit state; date-\(1\) absorption is allowed in the headline class.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent and identically distributed complete five-date panels \(O_i\) on the \(126\)-cell absorption-legal support.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort membership fixes the realized treatment path; no anticipation holds through date \(2\), and units absorbed by date \(1\) have identical absorbed potential continuations.
sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts and both latent types have positive probability; four-slice rank further implies positive active mass \(\alpha_j^d\) for each type and cohort.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is fitted. Empirical frequencies on the fixed \(126\)-cell support feed the guarded analytic contribution-recovery map.

prose_updates.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest causal setup and inverse-cancellation architecture, but their published full-rank and positive-transition hypothesis class excludes the common absorbing boundary; the present result is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of that class. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their respective time-homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; those scaling and label ideas are prior art, while the present theorem is a causal, time-varying active-minor result and does not subsume them. Restricted hidden-Markov measurement results likewise answer reconstruction questions under their own emission or structural restrictions, not the potential-path contribution identity proved here. Deaner and Ku (2026) motivate transition restrictions for absorbing duration outcomes but study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators; Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) provide neighboring Gaussian bootstrap and anti-concentration tools. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer: an incumbent-firm panel could use active productivity states and exit to study offsetting latent-type contributions, but this note does not claim their data satisfy its model or iid sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.interpretation:
The broad result separates three quantities that are often conflated. The full share \(\pi_j^d\) counts every member of latent type \(j\), including those already absorbed; the active share \(\alpha_j^d\) counts only members active at the recovery cut; and \(
u_j\) is the type's unnormalized contribution to the aggregate causal state shift. Active slices identify \(\alpha_j^d\), \(
u_j\), and the at-risk effect \(
u_j/\alpha_j^1\). They cannot determine which latent label owns already-absorbed zero-effect mass, so \(\pi_j^d\) and the full conditional \(	au_j\) need not be identified. If observed date-\(1\) absorption is absent, \(\alpha_j^d=\pi_j^d\), and the full conditional effects are recovered. Rao and Risch's setting is a motivation for this decomposition, not an empirical application carried out here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the efficiency bound for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated multinomial support-stratum model. It is not automatically the efficiency bound in the smaller fifth-date constrained Markov model. The latter uses the projected gradient only pointwise on smooth constant-rank strata, and the broad buffered class does not control constrained score rank or support changes. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed number of Monte Carlo draws needs a separate approximation error analysis. The sharp-frontier pair changes full latent type shares and full conditional type effects while preserving active shares, at-risk effects, both contribution vectors, and the entire aggregate ATT vector.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proposal proves a sufficient constructive frontier for two known latent types, two active states, one absorbing exit, four nonsingular matched active slices, simple common cycle signatures, cohort and type overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. It does not establish necessity beyond the explicit initial-absorption pair, identify unknown type count, handle weak eigengaps, justify clustered policy-panel inference, or allow approximate common transitions. Full conditional type effects require the observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface; the broad class identifies active sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate. Date-\(4\) common-kernel information is used only in the separately named constrained-efficiency subclass.
